events.event_title: US-China Tariff Escalation & Trade War Re-ignition
events.event_description: The Trump administration has reimposed aggressive tariffs on Chinese goods (up to 145%), with China retaliating at 125%+. This is actively disrupting supply chains, forcing sourcing shifts, and compressing margins for importers while benefiting domestic manufacturers and nearshoring plays. Quarterly earnings calls are now a live catalyst as companies quantify exposure.
events.rationale: POWL (Powell Industries) builds electrical equipment domestically and wins as reshoring accelerates. KTOS benefits from defense/domestic manufacturing tailwinds. ARCB (ArcBest) is a logistics mid-cap that could see volume shifts as trade routes reorganize. CEVA (semiconductor IP) has China revenue exposure making it a bearish second-order play. SGH (Smart Global Holdings) has direct Asia-sourced component risk with upcoming earnings as a catalyst.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $242 on tariff-escalation news + confirmation of domestic order acceleration in next earnings call, OR pullback to $228-232 on profit-taking with RSI <35 during peak trade-war headlines
tickers.exit_condition: Take profits at $260-265 on tariff policy reversal signals or Fed rate cut narrative shift; hard stop at $218 (break of 200-day MA) if domestic manufacturing demand disappoints in earnings
tickers.risk: Trump tariff policy reversal (deal negotiation), margin compression if raw material costs spike faster than pricing power materializes, or earnings miss if order pipeline weakens despite macro tailwinds; RSI at 39 suggests limited upside momentum currently

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $53.50 on tariff escalation headlines + defense spending acceleration confirmation, or dip to $50.80 on pullback with >2M volume
tickers.exit_condition: Take 50% at $56.00; trail stop at $51.20 for remainder. Exit full position if tariff negotiations show de-escalation or quarterly earnings miss defense growth expectations
tickers.risk: Tariff policy reversal/deal announcement removes catalyst; KTOS has China supply chain exposure that could offset domestic defense tailwinds; elevated RSI (49.2) suggests limited near-term momentum; broader market rotation out of defense cyclicals

tickers.entry_trigger: ARCB breaks above $152.50 resistance on tariff headline confirmation + volume surge, or dips to $148 on profit-taking for re-entry ahead of next earnings call
tickers.exit_condition: Exit at 165 or if tariff narrative reverses (deal/truce signals), or breach below 146 support on earnings miss or negative guidance on margin compression
tickers.risk: ARCB's domestic logistics exposure is indirect to tariff tailwinds; if demand destruction outweighs reshoring benefits, or if company lacks pricing power to offset fuel/labor costs, upside fails. China retaliation could also hurt ARCB's Asia-Pacific operations.

events.event_title: AI Data Center Power & Grid Infrastructure Buildout
events.event_description: Hyperscaler capex commitments for AI infrastructure remain at record levels ($300B+ combined 2025 guidance), creating acute demand for power equipment, transformers, cooling, and grid interconnection. Utility commission approvals and equipment delivery bottlenecks are the near-term catalysts, with multiple companies reporting earnings that will confirm order backlogs.
events.rationale: GEV (GE Vernova) is the premier grid equipment play with transformer backlog extending years. MYRG (MYR Group) is a mid-cap electrical contractor directly wiring data centers. NVEE (NV5 Global) does engineering/testing for grid projects. WATT (Energous) is speculative but levered to wireless power innovation. These are the picks-and-shovels beneath the headline Nvidia trade.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $245 on volume >2M shares, or pullback to $230-232 RSI <35 with confirmed earnings beat on backlog commentary
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $228, or if utility commission delays/grid capex guidance cuts materialize in earnings, or thesis crowding signals rotation to GEV/MYRG
tickers.risk: POWL is smaller-cap transformer/switchgear supplier vs. GEV's direct grid scale; execution risk on delivery timelines; multiple compression if Fed stays hawkish; supply chain normalization could deflate backlog premiums by Q3 2025

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $1,050 on volume >2M shares with confirmed Q4 earnings beat on transformer order backlog; or utility commission approval announcement for major grid interconnection project
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >70 with bearish divergence; or earnings miss on backlog conversion timeline; or supply chain relief reduces equipment scarcity premium; or AI capex guidance cuts from hyperscalers
tickers.risk: GEV valuation already elevated (~60-80x forward P/E typical for growth stocks); transformer delivery timelines slip; grid approval delays; competition from ABB/Siemens intensifies; macro recession reduces capex spending despite AI narrative

tickers.entry_trigger: RSI reversal above 40 on volume spike coinciding with utility commission approval announcements or major hyperscaler capex update; alternatively breach of $18.50 resistance
tickers.exit_condition: RSI >70 or +45% gain; or break below $15.00 on heavy volume; or if competing wireless power tech delays materialize within 8 weeks
tickers.risk: WATT is speculative and non-core to immediate AI data center build cycle—wireless power adoption lags transformer/cooling demand; valuation compression if broader semis/growth correct; company execution risk on commercialization timeline

events.event_description: Active US-brokered ceasefire talks create a bifurcated catalyst: a deal could pressure US defense stocks short-term while boosting European reconstruction plays, but failure or stalled talks sustains defense spending. Europe has committed to historic defense budget increases (3%+ GDP targets) regardless of outcome, with procurement contracts being awarded now.
events.rationale: KTOS (Kratos Defense) builds affordable drones/missiles aligned with modern warfare doctrine and European procurement needs. DRS (Leonardo DRS) is a mid-cap defense electronics specialist with NATO exposure. PLTR has active government contract momentum in both US and Allied nations. VEC (Vectrus, now V2X) handles base operations and reconstruction-adjacent contracts. AXON supplies law enforcement tech that scales into conflict-zone stabilization.

tickers.entry_trigger: KTOS breaks above $54.50 on volume >2M shares following European defense procurement announcement or contract award; RSI crosses above 55 on positive guidance revision
tickers.exit_condition: Ceasefire agreement signed with binding EU-Russia arms reduction clause; OR KTOS closes below $50.00; OR position reaches 4-month duration without catalyst catalyzation
tickers.risk: Sudden ceasefire breakthrough could trigger 8-12% defense stock rotation within days; KTOS reliance on European budget execution creates execution risk; domestic US defense budget uncertainty may pressure multiples despite international tailwinds

tickers.entry_trigger: PLTR breaks above $136.50 on volume >50M shares following European defense contract announcement or US government spending bill passage; alternatively, dip to $129-131 on ceasefire negotiation delay with RSI <45
tickers.exit_condition: Ceasefire agreement reached AND ratified (reduces defense urgency); OR PLTR closes below $128 on volume; OR 16-week timeframe expires without material NATO/EU contract wins; OR take 60% profits at $142 if target approaches
tickers.risk: Rapid ceasefire breakthrough deflates defense thesis; PLTR's valuation multiple vulnerable to rate hikes; geopolitical narrative shifts faster than contract cycles; European procurement delays; competition from specialized defense contractors (KTOS, DRS) capturing more upside

tickers.entry_trigger: AXON breaks below $530 on ceasefire deal announcement (risk-off flush) or holds $535+ if talks stall; accumulate on 3-5% pullback within next 2 weeks
tickers.exit_condition: Sell 50% at $565-570 on any ceasefire agreement; exit remaining position if AXON closes below $520 or if geopolitical catalyst loses market attention (>3 weeks without material news)
tickers.risk: AXON's law enforcement tech exposure is tangential to European defense rearmament; primary catalyst (Ukraine ceasefire) may not directly drive LE/stabilization contracts near-term; also vulnerable if US defense spending faces domestic pressure post-deal

events.event_title: GLP-1 Drug Supply Shortage Resolution & Obesity Market Expansion
events.event_description: FDA has declared the Ozempic/Wegovy shortage officially over, which ends compounding pharmacy production rights. This is an acute near-term bearish catalyst for compounders and telehealth platforms that built businesses on compounded semaglutide, while being bullish for branded manufacturers and medical device companies treating obesity comorbidities.
events.rationale: HIMS (Hims & Hers) faces existential pressure on its compounded GLP-1 revenue stream — a direct bearish catalyst with ongoing legal/regulatory deadlines. NKTR (Nektar) has pipeline assets in metabolic disease that could benefit from partnership interest. STVN (Stevanato) makes drug delivery devices and benefits from increased branded GLP-1 fill/finish volume. TMDX (TransMedics) sees reduced organ transplant need long-term as obesity declines — a slow-burn bearish second-order effect. ITCI has CNS pipeline but obesity-adjacent psychiatric comorbidity drugs gain attention.

tickers.entry_trigger: HIMS breaks below $35.50 on volume spike following FDA compounding guidance clarification or legal ruling against telehealth GLP-1 prescribing; RSI drops below 50
tickers.exit_condition: Close above $38.00 on recovery narrative (new non-GLP-1 revenue stream announced, partnership deal, or pivot to branded distribution); time stop at 6 weeks regardless
tickers.risk: Compounding revenue may be smaller than market fears; HIMS pivots successfully to branded GLP-1 distribution or obesity-adjacent services (mental health, cardiometabolic); short squeeze on crowded bearish positioning; FDA delays final ruling, creating uncertainty funk instead of capitulation

tickers.entry_trigger: NKTR closes above $68.50 on partnership announcement rumors or metabolic disease pipeline clinical data readout; volume confirmation >2M shares
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $64.80 OR no partnership materialization within 4 weeks OR broader biotech sector selloff (XBI -3%+)
tickers.risk: Thesis depends on speculative partnership interest—NKTR's pipeline has faced prior setbacks; GLP-1 shortage resolution benefits primarily large pharma (Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly), not smaller players; event catalyst timing undefined

tickers.entry_trigger: STVN breaks above $20.50 on volume >2M shares on news of major branded GLP-1 manufacturer securing fill/finish capacity expansion or earnings beat on device volume; alternatively dip to $18.50-$19.00 on market weakness with RSI <50 for lower-risk entry
tickers.exit_condition: Take profits at $22.50 or if RSI >70 without follow-through volume; stop loss at $18.20 (below recent support); exit full position after 4-6 weeks regardless of price if no material GLP-1 volume catalyst materializes
tickers.risk: STVN exposure to GLP-1 volume expansion is indirect and dependent on pharma capex cycles—may not see immediate revenue lift; competition from existing fill/finish capacity; broader biotech selloff could override sector tailwinds; obesity drug market maturation slower than expected; RSI already elevated at 65.7 reduces margin of safety
